Using a logistic regression of remission (Efficacy == PR vs SD/PD) on Age, BMI, and Gender (Male=1, Female=0) in the 80 valid records, the log-odds of remission decreases by approximately **−0.080 (−0.08) for each 1-year increase in patient age** (SE = 0.026, 95% CI −0.131 to −0.028, p = 0.0025; OR per year = exp(−0.0795) ≈ 0.92). Older age is significantly associated with lower odds of remission.

Full fitted model (n = 80; 41 remission/PR, 39 non-remission):
- Intercept: 1.5313 (SE 2.7755, p 0.581)
- **Age: −0.0795 per year (SE 0.0263, z −3.02, p 0.0025, 95% CI −0.1311 to −0.0280, OR 0.924)**
- BMI: 0.1621 per unit (SE 0.1088, p 0.136, OR 1.176)
- Gender Male vs Female: −0.6132 (SE 0.5471, p 0.262, OR 0.542)
Model converged; LLR p = 0.0033, pseudo R² = 0.124.

Explicit assumption: "remission" is operationalized as the Efficacy category PR (partial response), coded 1 = PR vs 0 = SD/PD, because the data contain only three efficacy categories (PR/SD/PD) and no CR/remission label. Under the alternative coding (disease control: PR+SD vs PD), the Age coefficient is similar in direction and magnitude (−0.0605, SE 0.0283, p 0.033, OR 0.941) — the negative age association is robust to the coding choice, though the coefficient value itself differs.
